articles.Heading: Week 11
articles.Title / Matchup: Week 11: San Diego State Unbeaten, but Virginia Holds the Top Line
articles.Text:
Welcome to the first Hardwood Sim bracketology. The committee (you) runs the weekly poll; this is the other half of the picture: who would be dancing if the season ended today, using results through Day 33.

The top line is Virginia (21-1), Alabama (20-1), San Diego State (22-0) and Utah St. (21-1). Virginia is the overall No. 1 seed: it has the best rating in the sim and a perfect 12-0 record in the ACC. San Diego State is unbeaten and now leads the Mountain West at 12-0, but its neighbor Utah St. rates far higher, 36.3 to 31.5. So I have the Aggies as my Mountain West auto-bid and the Aztecs as an at-large.

On auto-bids, I'm picking who I think cuts the nets down, not just who leads. Memphis gets the American's bid over UAB, which rates higher, because the Tigers lead the league at 11-2. Baylor gets the Big 12 nod over Texas Tech: level with Kansas at 11-2, with a top-10 rating. Alabama gets the SEC bid over Florida, which is 12-0 in the league, because of the rating gap. The Ivy League is wide open: Penn leads at 6-3, but Yale rates best.

The field is heavy on power leagues. The Big 12 and Big 10 have nine teams each, the ACC and SEC seven, and the Mountain West and Big East five. The last four in are UAB, Colorado, USC and Nebraska, who would open in the First Four. The first four out are NC State, Rutgers, Merrimack and Wichita State.

The notable absentees: Arizona is out. At 13-10 and 5-8 in the Big 12, it's hard to make a case. Michigan St. (4-7 in the Big 10) is out for the same reason. Pacific (20-2) and Richmond (20-3) are on the outside because of weak schedules and middling ratings.

Nine days remain in the regular season. Auto-bids will shift as conference races settle, and a bad week from a protected seed can open the door for a bubble team to leapfrog it. Watch Colorado and USC, who are in but barely, and Louisville, which is 21-1 but has a soft schedule. Next week's bracket will show who moved up, who dropped, and who entered or left the field.

articles.Heading: Week 12
articles.Title / Matchup: Week 12: Utah St. Topples San Diego State, and Three Auto-Bids Change Hands
articles.Text:
The biggest result of the week came on Day 35, when Utah St. beat San Diego State 98-91 in a Mountain West showdown. Both teams are 24-1 and 14-1 in league play, but the head-to-head win and Utah St.'s much better rating (37.6 to 31.3) keep the Aggies as my Mountain West auto-bid. The Aztecs fall from a No. 1 seed to a No. 2, in Virginia's region. Florida (24-1, 15-0 in the SEC) takes the open spot on the top line alongside Virginia (23-1, 14-0 in the ACC), Alabama (23-1, 14-0) and Utah St. Virginia stays the overall No. 1 seed. The SEC auto-bid stays with Alabama on the rating gap, even with both teams unbeaten in league play.

The Big 12 and Big 10 had the other big movement. Kansas beat Texas Tech 87-84 on Day 36 and moves up to a 2 seed, while Baylor beat West Virginia 79-67 and remains my Big 12 auto-bid at 14-2. Purdue is a perfect 14-0 in the Big 10 after blowing out Michigan (100-63) and Michigan St. (90-70), which lifts the Boilermakers from a 4 seed to a 2. Michigan also lost to USC, and USC jumps from the First Four to a 9 seed. Seton Hall beat Villanova twice, by 27 and by 41, rising to a 3 seed as the Wildcats fall four lines to a 12.

Three auto-bids changed hands. Winthrop beat Charleston Southern 65-61 on Day 36 and now leads the Big South by two and a half games, so the Eagles take that bid and Charleston Southern is out of the field. In the Ivy League, Princeton beat Yale 74-64 and leads at 7-2. I'm moving the bid from Yale (5-4) to Penn (8-3), who rates higher than Princeton. In the MAC, Ohio lost 83-75 to Northern Illinois and drops out of the bracket entirely. Massachusetts (12-3) takes the bid.

The at-large bubble shifted hard. Arizona (beat TCU on Day 35), Wichita State (13-2 in the American) and New Mexico (71-70 over Wyoming on Day 34) come in and join UAB in the First Four. Colorado and Nebraska go out. Colorado lost 87-59 to Iowa St. and is 6-10 in the Big 12. Nebraska was swept by Wisconsin, 104-88 and 101-62, and is 5-10 in the Big 10. Vanderbilt upset Texas 102-97 on Day 35 but still falls from a 12 seed to the First Four Out, with four bad losses and a 7-7 SEC record. Miami (lost to Duke), Rutgers, Vanderbilt and NC State, crushed 88-48 by Virginia Tech, are the first four out. Stanford (lost to Virginia and Florida State), Fresno State (beat Colorado State 83-80), Michigan St. and Merrimack are next. Richmond's hopes took a hit with losses to Davidson and Fordham, and the Spiders are off the board.

Six days remain. Virginia and Purdue are all but locked into their auto-bids. Cal State Fullerton (16-0), New Mexico State (15-0), Queens (14-0) and Tennessee St. (14-0) are in similar spots. Watch the American, where Memphis and Wichita State are tied at 13-2. Also watch the MAAC, where Merrimack (13-1) leads Saint Peter's (13-2), and the Ivy League, where Princeton and Penn are racing. The last four in, UAB, Wichita State, Arizona and New Mexico, are one bad loss from falling out, and Vanderbilt, Rutgers and Miami need wins to move in.

articles.Heading: Week 13
articles.Title / Matchup: Week 13: Alabama Stumbles, Florida Stays Perfect, and the Bubble Gets Ugly
articles.Text:
Good morning from Bracketology HQ. Three days left in the regular season, and the bracket is moving fast. Let's get right to it.

Start at the top. Virginia (26-1, 17-0 in the ACC) is still my No. 1 overall seed, and it isn't particularly close. Alabama's 101-88 loss to Texas on Day 39 is only its second of the year, and it keeps the Tide on the top line on résumé alone. But it does change the SEC auto-bid. Florida is 18-0 in league play after beating Texas 102-87 on Day 38 and Vanderbilt 96-74 on Day 39, so the Gators are my SEC pick, and Alabama is in as an at-large. That's the depth of this league. The other top seeds are Florida and Utah St. (27-1), which beat New Mexico and Colorado State on its way to 17-1 in the Mountain West. San Diego State took a 75-68 loss to UNLV on Day 38 and stays a 2 seed. UNLV moves up to a 3.

The Big 12 is a mess, and I mean that as a compliment. Texas Tech beat Baylor. Kansas State beat Kansas, and then beat Texas Tech 99-95 on Day 39. West Virginia knocked off Iowa St. and Baylor. Baylor has lost three straight (Texas Tech, BYU, West Virginia) and is 14-5 in league play. Kansas and West Virginia sit at 14-3, and I'm giving the Big 12 auto-bid to Kansas. Texas Tech and Kansas State both move up a line.

Purdue is 17-0 in the Big 10 after hammering Iowa 101-71. Indiana beat Michigan 74-72, and Michigan State beat Michigan too but lost to Illinois on Day 39. In the ACC, North Carolina won big over Miami (91-69) and Duke (97-75), and Duke drops two lines to a 6. Louisville fell 86-40 at Florida State, then lost to Stanford on Day 39, and slides two lines to an 11.

The one-bid leagues are producing dominoes. Delaware State beat Norfolk State 84-72 and leads the MEAC at 11-1, so it's my new MEAC bid. Incarnate Word beat Southeastern Louisiana on Day 39 and takes the Southland. Northern Illinois leads the MAC at 15-3 and takes the bid from Massachusetts, which drops out of the field. Evansville beat Valparaiso 83-78 to tie the MVC at 15-2, but I'm sticking with Valpo on talent. Pepperdine beat Gonzaga 72-71, and the Zags are 16-2 with a rival right behind them. Keep an eye on those leagues, because any upset in a one-bid league is a bid thief, and bid thieves are how bubbles die.

Now the bubble, and it's ugly. My last four in are TCU, which crushed BYU 95-65; Villanova; Wichita State, which lost 103-57 to UAB but is 15-3 in the American; and Rutgers, the last team in after beating Iowa on Day 39. First four out: Michigan State (7-10 in the Big 10), Miami (8-9 in the ACC, and that North Carolina loss didn't help), New Mexico (17-12, with losses to Utah St., Wyoming and Colorado State), and Fresno State, which lost 64-59 to San Diego State. NC State, Vanderbilt (lost by one to LSU, then by 22 to Florida), Dayton and Merrimack are next. I've listed the Locks, Safe teams and Bubble to the right.

Three days. Nothing is settled below the line. See you next week.

articles.Heading: Week 14
articles.Title / Matchup: Final Regular-Season Bracketology: Nine Perfect League Runs, a Brutal Bubble Week, and What to Watch in the Conference Tournaments
articles.Text:
Good morning from Bracketology HQ, and welcome to the last regular-season bracket of the year. The 30-game slate is in the books, and the final three days did real damage to the bubble. Here is the field, how we got here, and what I'll be watching when the conference tournaments tip.

THE TOP OF THE BOARD
Virginia (29-1) is my No. 1 overall seed, and it finished the job the right way: a perfect 20-0 in the ACC, with closing wins over Duke (87-68), Louisville (93-48) and Virginia Tech (108-60). Purdue matched it with its own 20-0 Big 10 run, sweeping Oregon and flattening Iowa 101-48, and that's enough to move the Boilermakers up to a 2 seed.

The game of the final day was Alabama 99, Florida 95. That result left the two tied at 19-1 atop the SEC, and I'm giving the auto-bid to the Tide on the head-to-head. Both are No. 1 seeds, joined by Utah St. (29-1, 19-1 in the Mountain West), which closed with a 93-69 win over Wyoming. The No. 2 line is Purdue, Texas, San Diego State and Iowa St. The Cyclones earned theirs with a 73-60 win over Texas Tech on Day 42. Seton Hall, Baylor, Texas Tech and UNLV are my 3 seeds.

HOW THE LEAGUES SHAKE OUT
Big 12 (9 bids): Kansas won the regular-season title at 17-3, Iowa St. (16-4) and Texas Tech (15-5) followed, and BYU, Arizona and TCU fill out the field. BYU (79-71 over West Virginia) and Arizona (82-79 over West Virginia) both landed 9 seeds.
ACC (8): Virginia, Florida State (28-2), North Carolina, Duke and Pittsburgh are comfortable. Virginia Tech is safe, and Louisville and Miami are hanging on.
Big 10 (8): Purdue, Indiana (26-4), Wisconsin and Michigan are solid. USC, Illinois, Oregon and Iowa are the soft spots of a league that went 8-12 for Michigan St. and sub-.500 for Nebraska.
SEC (6): Alabama, Florida, Texas, Arkansas, Missouri and Tennessee, which lost 87-71 to Oklahoma on Day 40 and sits at a 6.
Mountain West (6): Utah St., San Diego State and UNLV (both 18-2), Colorado State, Wyoming and, barely, Fresno State.
Big East (5): Seton Hall (27-3, 19-1), UConn, Xavier, Villanova and St. John's.
American (2): Memphis is the auto-bid at 18-2, with UAB the lone at-large.

THE BUBBLE: A BRUTAL FINAL WEEK
Here's where the last three days hurt. Wichita State was in my field last week. Then it lost 92-55 at East Carolina on the final day, and it's out. Rutgers also lost its final two games, to Michigan St. and USC, and slides to the Next Four Out. New Mexico lost 57-55 to Boise State on Day 42, and Merrimack lost to Siena and then by a single point to Mount St. Mary's, which ends its at-large case. Dayton, a 24-6 team, lost 95-60 to Davidson. Michigan St. closed 17-13, losing to Nebraska on Day 42 for an 8-12 Big 10 record, and it's gone.

My last four in are Louisville (24-6, but that 93-48 loss to Virginia hurts), TCU (8-12 in the Big 12, 95-94 loss to Texas Tech), Miami (10-10 in the ACC, beat Virginia Tech 79-78 and then lost to Duke) and Fresno State, the last team in, despite a 78-54 loss to UNLV. My first four out are Pepperdine (25-5, 18-2 in the WCC, three bad losses), Dayton, Vanderbilt (121-88 loss at Florida) and Evansville. Next four out: Colorado, Rutgers, NC State and Marquette. That's a lot of 19-11 teams with real flaws, and nobody is comfortable.

AUTO-BID CHANGES
Three of my picks flipped. Yale takes the Ivy bid in a three-way tie at 10-4 with Penn and Princeton, based on its 88-75 win over Penn on Day 41 and the best rating of the three. Southeastern Louisiana (17-3) takes the Southland from Incarnate Word. And Alabama takes the SEC. In the MEAC, Delaware State and Norfolk State both finished 12-2, and Norfolk won the last meeting 69-66. I'm sticking with Delaware State for the bid, but that one is a coin flip.

Nine teams in the field went unbeaten in league play: Virginia and Purdue, plus Cal State Fullerton, New Mexico State, Queens and Tennessee St. (all 20-0), Eastern Washington (18-0), New Hampshire (16-0) and Southern Utah (12-0).

WHAT TO WATCH IN THE CONFERENCE TOURNAMENTS
1. Bid thieves. I have 31 auto-bids and 37 at-large spots. Eleven of my auto-bid teams, Tennessee St., Valparaiso, New Mexico State, Cal State Fullerton, Southern Utah, Saint Peter's, Memphis, Queens, Eastern Washington, Coastal Carolina and Navy, have résumés that would at least get them into the bubble conversation if they lose. When one of them falls and someone else cuts the nets down, that's a second team from a one-bid league, and a bubble team loses a seat. Louisville, TCU, Miami and Fresno State should be rooting for chalk.
2. The league races that matter. The WCC is the biggest one: Pepperdine and Gonzaga both finished 18-2, and if the Waves win the title game, the Zags become an at-large and take a spot. The same applies to Evansville in the MVC, which beat Valpo and finished a game back. Dayton in the A-10 is the longshot.
3. The top line. Utah St. is one loss from handing a No. 1 seed to San Diego State or UNLV. The Alabama/Florida winner of the SEC tournament will also have a case for the top overall seed if Virginia stumbles, though that's unlikely.
4. The Big 12 and Big 10 at-larges. TCU needs to win a game, and Illinois, Oregon and Iowa can't afford an early exit.
5. The one-bid ties. The Ivy three-way and the MEAC tie will decide two bids.

That's the regular season. I'll be back after the tournaments with the real bracket. Until then, enjoy the chaos.

articles.Heading: Final
articles.Title / Matchup: Virginia Cuts Down the Nets: 39-1, a One-Point Escape in the Elite Eight, and a Bracket That Kept Breaking
articles.Text:
Good morning from Bracketology HQ, and congratulations to Virginia, your national champion. The Cavaliers beat Seton Hall 121-105 in the title game to finish 39-1, and they did it the hard way, with a bracket full of landmines. Let me take you through the whole thing.

THE CHAMPION
Virginia went 6-0 in the tournament and scored 111 points a game doing it. Five of its six wins came by double digits: 97-67 over North Dakota, 117-80 over UAB, 112-72 over Florida State, 113-103 over Texas in the Final Four, and 121-105 over Seton Hall in the final. The one scare was the Elite Eight, where Purdue, a perfect 20-0 team in the Big Ten, took the Cavaliers to the final possession and lost 106-105. That's the whole story of Virginia's year: a team that won its last 38 games in a row, and had to survive exactly one coin flip to get there. The best team in the sim won the title, and for a committee that put it at the top of the board all year, I'll take it.

THE FINAL FOUR
Three No. 1 seeds and a 2 made it to the last weekend. Virginia beat Texas, and Seton Hall edged Alabama 109-107 in the game of the tournament, a game that could have gone either way. The Pirates were the story of the second half of the bracket. They beat Northeastern 107-77, Saint Peter's 115-106 and New Mexico State 106-73, then won two straight by a total of three points, 80-79 over Virginia Tech and that 109-107 win over the Tide. They averaged nearly 104 points a game and still came up 16 short in the final. Alabama (35-4) and Texas (34-5) both ran into teams that simply scored more than they did.

THE ELITE EIGHT
It was a one-possession round. Virginia 106, Purdue 105. Seton Hall 80, Virginia Tech 79. Texas beat Michigan St. 84-80, and Alabama beat San Diego State 94-87. Two of the tournament's four one-point finishes came in this round.

THE SWEET 16 AND ROUND OF 32
The bracket cracked open on Day 50 and Day 51. Virginia Tech, an 8 seed, beat 1 seed Utah St. 99-93, the team that had lost only twice all year, and then beat North Carolina 78-77. New Mexico State, an 11 seed, beat Texas Tech 91-89. Eastern Washington, a 13, beat West Virginia. Michigan St. beat UC Irvine 76-66 and then 2 seed Florida 83-80. San Diego State beat Baylor in the Sweet 16, and Duke handled Kansas 79-63 before Alabama ended its run, 109-72.

THE UPSET TALLY
Twenty of the 63 games after the First Four went to the lower seed. Twelve of them came in the first round, four in the round of 32, three in the Sweet 16 and one in the Final Four, when 2 seed Seton Hall beat 1 seed Alabama. The Elite Eight and the title game went chalk. The tournament averaged a 16.7-point margin, and nine games were decided by three points or fewer. The only two games decided by 40 or more were Purdue's 115-68 win over Vermont and Virginia's 112-72 win over Florida State.

THE CINDERELLAS
Michigan St. is the one I'll remember. The Spartans were 18-14 with an 8-12 Big Ten record, one of the last two at-large teams in the field, and they went to Dayton and won four games to reach the Elite Eight. They beat Wyoming, Indiana, UC Irvine and Florida before a four-point loss to Texas ended the run. The committee took a lot of heat for that selection, and the Spartans answered it. Virginia Tech was the other one. A 24-10 team that went to the ACC final, it beat a 1 seed and a 4 seed and then lost to eventual finalist Seton Hall by a single point. New Mexico State, which also came out of Dayton, won three games, and Eastern Washington, a 13 seed, beat West Virginia to reach the Sweet 16. Credit those four.

THE BUSTS
Utah St. (31-2) is the biggest. A No. 1 seed, 30 points a game in margin, and gone in the second round. Iowa St. and UNLV, both 3 seeds, lost to 14 seeds in the first round, Penn over UNLV 86-81 and UC Irvine over the Cyclones 81-66. Every 7 seed went home in round one, and the 12 seeds went 0-4. Tennessee St., the 32-1 team that I circled as my upset special, lost to Missouri by 17.

THE CONFERENCES
The ACC won 16 games, the most of any league, powered by Virginia's six and Virginia Tech's three. The SEC won 11 and the Big Ten 10, with Michigan St. and Purdue doing most of the work. The Big East got five wins from Seton Hall alone, and the Mountain West won five games, three of them San Diego State's.

HOW MY BRACKET HELD UP
I got the champion right, and I had two of the four Final Four teams, Virginia and Alabama. I missed on Texas and Seton Hall, because I had Florida and Utah St. there instead, and both went out early. By round I was 20 of 32, 10 of 16, 6 of 8 and 2 of 4, so 38 of 60 through the Elite Eight, with the right winner at the end. That's a bracket that was good where the top seeds mattered and wrong wherever a 7-10 or a 13 seed got hot.

THE BOTTOM LINE
This was a tournament of one-possession games, a champion who earned it, and a last-team-in that nearly made the Final Four. If you want to know what to take from it, here it is: the best team won, and nobody should ever tell you that a bubble team can't make a run. See you next season.

articles.Heading: First Four Game 1
articles.Text: DAYTON, GAME 1. Arkansas-Pine Bluff (23-10) cruised in the SWAC final, 69-49, but it carries six bad losses. Winthrop (23-10) comes in on a 14-game winning streak after going 15-1 in the Big South, and it allows just 66.7 a night. UAPB needs to get to the line and make Winthrop shoot over the top; Winthrop needs to keep this in the 60s, where it lives. The winner gets Alabama, so nobody's looking past Tuesday. MY PICK: Winthrop.

articles.Heading: First Four Game 2
articles.Text: DAYTON, GAME 2. This is the matchup the bubble folks love. New Mexico State (29-3, a perfect 20-0 in C-USA) has the record; Illinois (19-12) has the schedule, the best strength of schedule in the First Four at +11.7. Same rating, 16.2 apiece. State needs to prove a soft-schedule résumé travels. Illinois needs to take care of the ball, since it enters 5-5 in its last 10. The winner gets Arkansas. MY PICK: New Mexico State.

articles.Heading: First Four Game 3
articles.Text: DAYTON, GAME 3. The lowest-rated pairing in the field, and that's no insult, it's what makes it fun. Liberty (24-10) won the C-USA tournament as a 5 seed on the strength of a defense that allows 62.4 a night. North Dakota (22-11) has won five straight and beat Oral Roberts for the Summit title. Liberty's defense is the safer bet; North Dakota needs to shoot the lights out. The winner draws Virginia. MY PICK: Liberty.

articles.Heading: First Four Game 4
articles.Text: DAYTON, GAME 4. Wyoming (22-10) has the better record and a win over North Carolina. Michigan State (18-14, 8-12 in the Big Ten) has the better rating (17.2 to 15.5) and the Big Ten schedule, but it has lost six of its last 10. The Spartans need their offense to show up; Wyoming needs to keep the turnovers down and win the rebounding battle. The winner gets Indiana. MY PICK: Michigan State.

articles.Heading: East (1) vs (16)
articles.Text: The overall No. 1 seed against the Dayton winner. Virginia (33-1) has won 32 in a row and scores 104 a night, so the 16 seed needs to do two things: slow the game way down and hold on to the ball. Liberty's defense (62.4 allowed) is built for the first; nobody is built for the second. Nobody in this field is a bigger favorite. MY PICK: Virginia.

articles.Heading: East (8) vs (9)
articles.Text: Xavier (20-12) has the schedule (+9.2) and a win over UConn. UAB (26-7) has the hot hand: 10-0 in its last 10, 93.5 points a game, and the better rating (22.3 to 18.3). Xavier needs to make this a half-court game and get stops. UAB just needs to keep doing what it's doing. Xavier is 4-6 in its last 10, and that tells you where the momentum is. MY PICK: UAB.

articles.Heading: East (5) vs (12)
articles.Text: Kansas State (23-8) has been through the Big 12 gauntlet (+10.7 strength of schedule) with three top-25 wins. Coastal Carolina (30-3) allows just 63 a game and went 18-2 in the Sun Belt, but it hasn't played anyone close to this. K-State needs to avoid the early letdown. The Chanticleers need to prove 30 wins against softer competition (-4.8) can scale. Respect the 12, but not too much. MY PICK: Kansas State.

articles.Heading: East (4) vs (13)
articles.Text: Florida State (29-3) scores 90 and allows 66, a +24 margin. Navy (28-5) is 10-0 in its last 10 and went 17-1 in the Patriot League, but its schedule (-2.5) has no top-50 wins. The Midshipmen need threes and a slow game; the Seminoles need to remember their quarterfinal loss to Virginia Tech and come out sharp. MY PICK: Florida State.

articles.Heading: East (6) vs (11)
articles.Text: Wisconsin (25-7, 15-5 in the Big Ten) scores 88 but allows 76, so it's always going to be a shootout. BYU (18-13) has four top-25 wins, the most in the pod, and four bad losses, so it's anyone's guess. The Cougars need the version that beat Baylor. The Badgers need to play some defense. If BYU's shots fall, this is an upset. MY PICK: Wisconsin.

articles.Heading: East (3) vs (14)
articles.Text: UNLV (30-3) is the Mountain West champion, allows 60 a night, and is 10-0 in its last 10. Penn (24-9) won the Ivy title game 76-68 and scores 83 a game, but it has four bad losses and no top-50 wins. The Quakers need a barrage of threes and a slow UNLV start. The Rebels have the best defense of any 3 seed. MY PICK: UNLV.

articles.Heading: East (7) vs (10)
articles.Text: Tennessee (23-8) has three top-25 wins and went 14-6 in the SEC, but it's 5-5 in its last 10 and lost its SEC tournament opener. Villanova (22-10) has a +10.6 schedule and four second-tier wins, but nothing against the top. The Vols need their defense (68 allowed) back; the Wildcats need to win the three-point battle. MY PICK: Tennessee.

articles.Heading: East (2) vs (15)
articles.Text: Purdue (31-3) went a perfect 20-0 in the Big Ten, has a 29-game winning streak, and won the tournament by an average of more than 20 a game. Vermont (24-9) knocked off New Hampshire for the America East title and has a win over West Virginia, so it knows how to win as an underdog. The Catamounts need to shoot over 40% from deep and rebound. Purdue needs to avoid the one-bad-night loss. MY PICK: Purdue.

articles.Heading: South (1) vs (16)
articles.Text: Texas (30-4) just beat Alabama in the SEC final and scores 98 a night. Delaware State (27-6) has a -8.3 strength of schedule, the weakest in the field, and three bad losses. The Hornets need an enormous shooting night and need to keep the Longhorns off the glass. Texas needs to be careful with the ball. MY PICK: Texas.

articles.Heading: South (8) vs (9)
articles.Text: New Hampshire (30-3) went 16-0 in the America East and outscores teams by 27 a night, but its schedule is -5.7 and it lost the conference title game to Vermont. Pittsburgh (24-8) has no bad losses and a +9.5 schedule, but no signature win either. New Hampshire needs to prove the numbers are real. Pitt needs to turn this into a rock fight. MY PICK: New Hampshire.

articles.Heading: South (5) vs (12)
articles.Text: West Virginia (25-9) has six top-25 wins, the most of any 5 seed, and reached the Big 12 final. Southern Utah (27-5) went 12-0 in the WAC, has a 16-game winning streak, and allows just 65. This is an upset alert. The Mountaineers need to protect the ball against a defense that sits back; the Thunderbirds need to make the favorites uncomfortable. MY PICK: West Virginia.

articles.Heading: South (4) vs (13)
articles.Text: UConn (26-7) was crushed 104-71 by Seton Hall in the Big East final, and it needs to reset. Eastern Washington (27-6) went 18-0 in the Big Sky, has won 22 straight, and has a win over Oregon. The Eagles need to rebound and shoot; the Huskies have eight second-tier wins and no bad losses, so the floor is high. MY PICK: UConn.

articles.Heading: South (6) vs (11)
articles.Text: Indiana (27-5) has eight wins over top-50 teams and no bad losses. The Dayton winner is dangerous, either a Wyoming team with a win over North Carolina or a Michigan State team that has seen the Big Ten. The Hoosiers need to keep the defense (67 allowed) and score late. Indiana lost its Big Ten quarterfinal to Maryland, so a sloppy start would be a warning sign. MY PICK: Indiana.

articles.Heading: South (3) vs (14)
articles.Text: Iowa State (27-6) has five top-25 wins and no bad losses. UC Irvine (26-7) won the Big West and allows 65 a night, but it has four bad losses and a -5.6 schedule. The Anteaters need to slow the game down and win the possession battle. The Cyclones need to finish what they started in the Big 12 tournament. MY PICK: Iowa State.

articles.Heading: South (7) vs (10)
articles.Text: Two champions, both 29-4, both 18-2. Gonzaga (rating 24.0) allows 62.5 a night, while Valparaiso (17.1) has the better win of the pair, over Seton Hall. Valpo needs to win the three-point battle. Gonzaga needs to avoid getting dragged into a slugfest and use its size inside. The Zags have the edge in talent. MY PICK: Gonzaga.

articles.Heading: South (2) vs (15)
articles.Text: Florida (30-3) scores 104 a night and outscores opponents by 30. Mount St. Mary's (21-12) beat Saint Peter's twice and won the MAAC title game 75-71, but it has five bad losses. The Mountaineers need to keep it low and slow and make threes; the Gators need to play some defense (73.8 allowed). MY PICK: Florida.

articles.Heading: West (1) vs (16)
articles.Text: Alabama (31-3) has six top-25 wins and scores 104 a night. The 16 seed will come out of Dayton, either an Arkansas-Pine Bluff team with six bad losses or a Winthrop team on a 14-game streak. Whoever it is needs to keep Alabama's pace under control and shoot over the top. The Crimson Tide just need to be Alabama. MY PICK: Alabama.

articles.Heading: West (8) vs (9)
articles.Text: Wofford (30-3) is 10-0 in its last 10, allows 63, and is the most dangerous 8 seed in the bracket. Colorado State (23-9) scores 86.7 but allows 77.4, and it has no bad losses. The Terriers' strength of schedule (-2.0) is the question; they have no top-50 wins. The Rams need a high-scoring game. MY PICK: Wofford.

articles.Heading: West (5) vs (12)
articles.Text: Duke (26-7) has eight second-tier wins and a +10.9 schedule. St. John's (19-12, 10-10 in the Big East) has lost two straight and is 5-5 in its last 10, but it has no bad losses. The Red Storm need to turn Duke over and make threes. The Blue Devils need to come out with energy after a semifinal loss to Virginia. MY PICK: Duke.

articles.Heading: West (4) vs (13)
articles.Text: Kansas (28-4) has four top-25 wins and no bad losses. Queens (30-3) went 20-0 in the ASUN and has won 24 straight, but its -7.3 strength of schedule is the weakest of any team seeded this high. The Royals need to hit their threes and keep it close. The Jayhawks need to shake off an early Big 12 tournament exit. MY PICK: Kansas.

articles.Heading: West (6) vs (11)
articles.Text: Michigan (25-8) has six wins over top-50 teams. Oregon (20-11) allows 78.5 a night and is 4-6 in its last 10. The Ducks have a +10.3 schedule, and they need to win a track meet. The Wolverines need to bounce back after a 104-64 loss to Purdue in the Big Ten semifinals. MY PICK: Michigan.

articles.Heading: West (3) vs (14)
articles.Title / Matchup: (3) San Diego State (32-4) vs (14) Northern Illinois (27-7)
articles.Text: San Diego State (29-3) has the toughest schedule of any 3 seed (+11.4) and a win over Purdue. Northern Illinois (27-6) has won 16 straight, but it has five bad losses and no top-50 wins. The Huskies need to keep it close early and shoot well. The Aztecs need to avoid a slow start. MY PICK: San Diego State.

articles.Heading: West (7) vs (10)
articles.Text: St. Louis (29-2) scores 91 and allows 65, but its schedule (-0.7) is the question, and it lost its A-10 opener to Fordham. Louisville (26-7) has a win over North Carolina, but it's 5-5 in its last 10 and has the lowest rating of any at-large team in the West. The Cardinals need to slow it down. The Billikens need to prove they belong. MY PICK: St. Louis.

articles.Heading: West (2) vs (15)
articles.Text: Baylor (29-5) won the Big 12 tournament by beating Texas Tech, Arizona and West Virginia, and has five top-25 wins. IU Indy (27-6) has won 19 straight, and went through the Horizon tournament with two one-possession wins. The Jaguars need a game like the Robert Morris one. The Bears need to take them seriously. MY PICK: Baylor.

articles.Heading: Midwest (1) vs (16)
articles.Text: Utah State (31-2) scores 97 a night and outscores opponents by 30. Its only two losses were both to UNLV. Southeastern Louisiana (23-10) has four bad losses and no win over a top-100 team. The Lions need to slow the pace and hit threes. The Aggies need to put it away early. MY PICK: Utah State.

articles.Heading: Midwest (8) vs (9)
articles.Text: Virginia Tech (24-10) made the ACC final as a No. 7 seed; USC (22-9) is 8-2 in its last 10 and has a win over Michigan. The Hokies need to hold the defense (70 allowed) and play after four games in four days. The Trojans need to avoid the early Big Ten tournament exit they had. This one is close to a coin flip. MY PICK: Virginia Tech.

articles.Heading: Midwest (5) vs (12)
articles.Text: Here's the one I'm circling. Missouri (27-5) is a very good team, 16-4 in the SEC with a win over Texas. But Tennessee State (32-1) went 20-0 in the Ohio Valley, has won 24 straight, and allows just 61 a night. The schedule (-8.3) is the red flag, but the numbers are too good to ignore. Tigers versus Tigers; the Missouri guards need to protect the ball. MY PICK: Tennessee State, my upset special.

articles.Heading: Midwest (4) vs (13)
articles.Text: North Carolina (27-5) has six wins over top-50 teams and no bad losses. Dayton (27-6) won the A-10 title game 96-66 and has the best strength of schedule of any 13 seed (+1.3). The Flyers need to disrupt and make threes. The Tar Heels need to keep their feet on the gas after a quarterfinal loss to Louisville. MY PICK: North Carolina.

articles.Heading: Midwest (6) vs (11)
articles.Title / Matchup: (6) Arkansas (26-8) vs (11) New Mexico State / Illinois
articles.Text: Arkansas (26-7) scores 90 and allows 75, a team built for shootouts. The Dayton winner is a live underdog either way, a New Mexico State team that went 29-3 or an Illinois team with the toughest schedule of any First Four team. The Razorbacks need to defend. This is a 6 seed that can be had. MY PICK: Arkansas.

articles.Heading: Midwest (3) vs (14)
articles.Text: Texas Tech (25-7) scores 92 a night and outscores teams by 21. Le Moyne (28-5) allows just 61.8, is 10-0 in its last 10, and has a 12-game winning streak, but it has three bad losses and a -7.1 schedule. The Dolphins need to slow the game to a crawl. The Red Raiders need to make shots. MY PICK: Texas Tech.

articles.Heading: Midwest (7) vs (10)
articles.Text: Arizona (22-11) beat Kansas in the Big 12 tournament and has been hot, winning nine of its last 10. Saint Peter's (28-5, 18-2 in the MAAC) has no bad losses, but it has no top-50 wins either. The Peacocks need to prove they belong; the Wildcats need to avoid a slow start. MY PICK: Arizona.

articles.Heading: Midwest (2) vs (15)
articles.Text: Seton Hall (30-3) has won 22 straight, scored 104 in the Big East final, and has 12 wins over top-50 teams. Northeastern (27-6) has five bad losses and a best win over #109 Stonehill. The Huskies need to hit everything. The Pirates need to take care of business. MY PICK: Seton Hall.

articles.Heading: East 1
articles.Text: The overall No. 1 and the class of the field: 33-1, a perfect 20-0 in the ACC, and 104 points a game. To cut down the nets, Virginia just has to avoid a one-night shooting slump and keep the defense (70 allowed) at the level it has been all year. The only real risk is a slow, ugly game against a defense that can keep it in the 60s.

articles.Heading: East 2
articles.Text: 31-3, a perfect 20-0 in the Big Ten, and a 29-game winning streak. The Boilermakers need to keep scoring at nearly 89 a game and avoid a one-bad-night loss. The best 2 seed in the bracket, and a potential Elite Eight date with Virginia.

articles.Heading: East 3
articles.Text: 30-3, the Mountain West champion, allowing just 60 a night, and 10-0 in its last 10. It beat Utah State 79-78 for the title. The most underrated 3 seed in the bracket, UNLV needs guard play late in close games.

articles.Heading: East 4
articles.Text: 29-3, scoring 90.5 and allowing 66.2. The Seminoles need to show their quarterfinal loss to Virginia Tech was a blip and get their guards through the opening weekend. They have the profile of a Sweet 16 team.

articles.Heading: East 5
articles.Text: 23-8 with three top-25 wins, including one over Texas Tech. To go deep, the Wildcats must avoid the kind of early letdown they had in the Big 12 tournament and lean on their experience. Their schedule (+10.7) says they're ready.

articles.Text: 25-7 and 15-5 in the Big Ten, scoring 88 but allowing 76. To advance, the Badgers must defend. The offense will show up on its own.

articles.Text: 23-8 and 14-6 in the SEC, with a win over Texas. To get past the opening weekend, the Vols need to snap a 5-5 finish and find the defense (68 allowed) that carried them in January.

articles.Text: 20-12 with no bad losses, a +9.2 schedule, and a win over UConn. Xavier needs to snap a 4-6 skid and bring the offense that carried it to the Big East semifinals. If it defends, it can beat UAB.

articles.Heading: East 9
articles.Text: 26-7, the American champion, scoring 93.5 a night and 10-0 in its last 10. To make a run, UAB has to keep scoring in transition and avoid a slow start. It's the team nobody wants to see as a 9 seed.

articles.Heading: East 10
articles.Text: 22-10, a +10.6 schedule, and four second-tier wins. To advance, Villanova needs to take care of the ball and win the three-point battle. It lost a two-point game to UConn in the Big East semifinals.

articles.Heading: East 11
articles.Text: 18-13, with four top-25 wins and four bad losses. A true wild card: if BYU plays the way it did against Baylor, it can beat anyone in this region. If it doesn't, it goes home early.

articles.Heading: East 12
articles.Text: 30-3, the Sun Belt champion, allowing 62.5 a night. To pull the upset, the Chanticleers need to grind the game down, make their threes, and win the possession battle. Nobody has tested them like this.

articles.Text: 28-5, the Patriot champion, with a 20-game winning streak entering the field. To win, Navy needs to hit from the outside and not get overwhelmed by athleticism. The streak says they can handle pressure.

articles.Text: A 24-10 defensive team (62.4 allowed) that won the C-USA tournament as a 5 seed. To make noise, Liberty has to win Dayton and then slow a top seed to a crawl. It will need to make threes at a clip it hasn't all year.

articles.Text: 30-4, the SEC tournament champion, scoring 98 a night with seven top-25 wins. To win it all, the Longhorns have to defend a little better (73 allowed) and play a guard-driven game in the half court.

articles.Heading: South 2
articles.Text: 30-3, scoring 104 a night, and 19-1 in the SEC. To win it all, the Gators need to play some defense (73.8 allowed). No team in the field scores more.

articles.Heading: South 3
articles.Text: 27-6, with five top-25 wins and no bad losses. To go deep, the Cyclones need to finish games better, as they showed in a six-point loss to West Virginia in the Big 12 tournament. They have the résumé of a title contender.

articles.Heading: South 4
articles.Text: 26-7, with eight second-tier wins and a +11.2 schedule. To make a run, the Huskies need to reset after a 33-point loss to Seton Hall in the Big East final. If they bounce back, they're a 4 seed with a high floor.

articles.Heading: South 5
articles.Text: 25-9, with six top-25 wins and a trip to the Big 12 final. To go deep, the Mountaineers need to protect the ball against teams that sit back and defend. They have the résumé of a Sweet 16 team.

articles.Text: 27-5, 17-3 in the Big Ten, with eight top-50 wins and no bad losses. To advance, the Hoosiers need to keep the defense (67 allowed) and score late in games. A sloppy start would be the warning sign.

articles.Heading: South 7

articles.Text: 30-3 and a perfect 16-0 in the America East, but it lost the conference title game to Vermont. To win, the Wildcats must prove that a 27-point margin against a soft schedule (-5.7) is real.

articles.Heading: South 9

articles.Text: 31-3 and 19-1 in the SEC, with six top-25 wins and 104 points a night. To win the title, the Crimson Tide need to keep their pace and avoid a defensive lapse (76 allowed). They lost the SEC final to Texas, so there's a little fire there.
